script: [serious] July 1518. Strasbourg. A woman named Frau Troffea steps into the street... and starts to dance. No music. No reason. She dances for days. Within a week, more than thirty people have joined her. By August, some accounts say hundreds. They danced until their feet bled. Some collapsed from exhaustion. And the city's response? [whispers] More dancing. The council believed the cure was to dance it out. They opened up guildhalls, built a stage, and hired musicians to keep everyone going. It made things worse. Finally, they banned public music and sent the dancers to a mountain shrine, to pray to Saint Vitus, in red shoes. Slowly, it stopped. What caused it? The leading theory: a city pushed to its breaking point by famine and disease... and a mass panic of the mind. Others blame poisoned grain. Nobody knows for sure. This is Dossier Decoded. Case file number six. Which file should we open next?
